source: Create a realistic city driving map for a car game. The city should have a grid layout of streets with the following elements: - A ground/base plate representing asphalt roads forming a grid pattern with intersections - Buildings of varying heights on the blocks between roads (some tall, some medium, some short) - Sidewalks along the edges of roads - Road markings (lane dividers, crosswalks at intersections) - Street lights at intersections - Trees or small vegetation on some sidewalks - Parking lots or open spaces in some blocks Make it look realistic with appropriate colors: dark gray asphalt, gray sidewalks, varied building colors (browns, grays, blues), green trees. Expose the following configurable attributes: - blockSize: size of each city block (controls building area) - roadWidth: width of the roads - gridCount: number of blocks in the grid (controls overall map size) - buildingHeightMin: minimum building height - buildingHeightMax: maximum building height - treeDensity: how many trees to place along sidewalks - streetLightSpacing: distance between street lights
scene_prompt: Create a realistic 3D city driving map organized as a grid of asphalt streets and intersections. City blocks between the roads contain buildings of varied heights—tall, medium, and short—in brown, gray, and blue tones, with some blocks used for parking lots or open open spaces. Gray sidewalks border every road, with green trees or small vegetation placed along selected sidewalks. Use dark gray asphalt with lane dividers and crosswalks at intersections, and place street lights at intersections. Size the overall grid, blocks, roads, building-height range, tree density, and street-light spacing to be configurable.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is `Simulation`, specifically a Vehicle Sim: players drive through a persistent city rather than race toward laps or a finish line.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-open`, a single contiguous drivable city grid whose streets can be explored in any order. This matches the Vehicle Sim preset in shape, but use only the road-network aspect; the preset’s extraction field is not present.

### Config requirements
Use `path-road-vehicle` for a connected, vehicle-width rectilinear street grid with regular intersections. Use `settlement-density` for dense urban blocks filled with varied-height buildings, while selected blocks remain parking lots or open spaces. Road width, block size, grid count, minimum and maximum building height, tree density, and street-light spacing remain configurable scene dimensions. Draw dark-gray asphalt, gray sidewalks, lane dividers, crosswalks, intersection street lights, and scattered green sidewalk vegetation.

### Layout requirements
No separate placed gameplay markers are required; this prompt specifies the drivable built environment only.

### Layout components
Build a configurable square or rectangular grid of asphalt roads, with each block bounded by sidewalks and each intersection marked by crosswalks, lane dividers, and street lights. Fill most intervening blocks with brown, gray, and blue buildings distributed across tall, medium, and short height bands. Reserve some complete blocks for parking lots or open open spaces. Place trees or low vegetation along selected sidewalk runs according to the configurable tree density, and repeat street lights along roads according to the configurable spacing, with mandatory lights at intersections. The city boundary is the outermost road-and-block ring; frame the full grid clearly from an elevated three-quarter view.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the visual realism and urban massing lead, while the top-down plan is projected from the rendered grid.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, expanding or contracting with configurable `gridCount`. Theme: realistic contemporary city driving environment, dark asphalt, neutral concrete, muted brown/gray/blue buildings, and green streetscape. Use `P0`; the city is one connected ground surface with no forced multi-layer, interior, or topology-validation pass.
